quickAnswerTitle: How Oregon School Calendars Work in 2026–27
quickAnswer: Oregon does not use one statewide K–12 calendar. Local school boards set the days and hours when schools are in session, while state rules establish minimum instructional hours by grade level. First days, breaks, conference closures, early-release schedules, staff days, possible make-up days, and last days therefore vary by district. MySchoolDates currently has reviewed calendars for Portland Public Schools, Beaverton School District, and Salem-Keizer Public Schools.
about:
Oregon school calendars are set locally rather than through one statewide schedule. Oregon law gives district school boards authority to fix the days of the year and hours of the day when schools are in session. As a result, neighboring districts can use different first days, breaks, conference schedules, early-release patterns, staff days, and last days.

Oregon also measures the school year through minimum instructional hours instead of requiring every district to use the same number of student days. Current state requirements are 900 hours for kindergarten through grade 8, 990 hours for grades 9–11, and 966 hours for grade 12 for the required share of students. That distinction matters when comparing calendars: a shorter day, conference schedule, or staff-development date cannot be interpreted from the date label alone.

The reviewed Portland and Beaverton calendars illustrate why district-level detail matters. PPS uses staged openings, Kindergarten Ramp Up, level-specific early release, and conference closures. Beaverton uses a 174-day district calendar, a grade-level first-day caveat, a separate 135-day Pre-K calendar with no Friday classes, and a conditional June make-up week. Families should choose the correct district and program before relying on any date.
calendarRulesDescription: Oregon combines locally adopted district calendars with statewide instructional-time and school-holiday rules. These are the distinctions families are most likely to encounter.

calendarRules.label: District boards set calendars
calendarRules.description: Oregon district school boards set the days and hours when schools are in session, so there is no single statewide first day, spring break, or last day.

calendarRules.label: Instruction is measured in hours
calendarRules.description: State rules set minimum annual instructional hours by grade level. A district calendar should not be judged only by counting dates or assuming a universal 180-day requirement.

calendarRules.label: Presidents Day is not automatic
calendarRules.description: Oregon law does not designate Presidents Day as a legal school holiday. A district may still close or schedule a staff day, so families must check the local calendar.

calendarRules.label: Year-round schedules are permitted
calendarRules.description: Oregon law allows a district board to adopt a schedule that operates throughout the year for some or all schools. Confirm the calendar assigned to a specific school or program.

calendarRules.label: Instructional time is protected
calendarRules.description: Oregon's 2026 instructional-time order prevents districts and public charter schools from further reducing student instructional time and establishes restoration requirements for districts that reduced time.

calendarRules.label: School details may differ
calendarRules.description: Districtwide calendars may not include every bell time, alternative-program opening, conference schedule, athletics date, or school-specific event.

stateSections.label: Oregon Instructional-Time Requirements
stateSections.content:
Oregon's minimums apply to at least 92% of students in a district. State rules allow limited amounts of qualifying recess, staff professional development, and parent-teacher conference time to count toward the calculation, so a calendar's visible student days do not tell the whole story.

In April 2026, Oregon issued an order preserving student instructional time. Districts and public charter schools may not further reduce student instructional time, and districts that reduced time must address restoration requirements for 2027–28. Families should still use the locally adopted calendar for actual attendance dates.

Do not assume Presidents Day is a statewide day off for Oregon students. Check whether the district lists a closure, staff day, or regular school day.
Treat possible snow or emergency make-up dates as conditional until the district announces that they will be used.

faqs.q: When do Oregon public schools start in 2026?
faqs.a: Oregon does not have one statewide first day of school. Local district boards set their calendars, so 2026–27 opening dates vary by district and may also differ by grade or program. Portland Public Schools starts most students August 26, 2026, while Beaverton School District lists August 25 and notes that grade-level dates may be modified.

faqs.q: Are Oregon school calendars the same statewide?
faqs.a: No. Oregon district school boards set the days and hours when their schools are in session. Winter break, spring break, conference days, early-release schedules, staff days, possible make-up days, and the last day can all differ by district.

Oregon's statewide standard is based on minimum instructional hours by grade level, not one universal 180-day calendar. Current minimums are 900 hours for kindergarten through grade 8, 990 hours for grades 9–11, and 966 hours for grade 12 for the required share of students.

faqs.q: When is Oregon Spring Break in 2027?
faqs.a: There is no single statewide Oregon Spring Break. Each district adopts its own dates, so families should select the district calendar and verify the official break before arranging travel or child care.

faqs.q: Are Oregon schools closed on Presidents Day?
faqs.a: Not automatically. Oregon law says Presidents Day is not a legal school holiday. Individual districts may still list a closure, staff day, conference day, or other schedule change, so check the local district calendar.

faqs.q: Can weather change an Oregon school calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. Districts may identify possible make-up dates or revise the last day after weather or emergency closures. A reserved date remains conditional until the district announces that it will be used.

faqs.q: Can I add an Oregon school calendar to Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. Reviewed MySchoolDates district pages provide an ICS file that can be imported into Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook. The file is a one-time import rather than a live district subscription, so later district changes do not update automatically.
